subject.title: fix: scope native hook relay processes

question: Should native hook relay scoping become a default Linux command wrapper, or must it be opt-in or viability-checked before merge?
rationale: This changes a native hook enforcement path with compatibility, availability, and security-boundary impact; the safe default is a maintainer product and upgrade decision, not only a code-style choice.

options.title: Require fail-safe scoping
options.body: Use systemd scoping only after proving the exact constrained scope can start and preserve hook stdio, otherwise keep the original relay command.

options.title: Accept default scoping with proof
options.body: Accept the new Linux default only after redacted real Linux proof shows scoped relay execution and fallback behavior both work.

options.title: Defer to canonical relay work
options.body: Pause or close this branch if maintainers prefer idle-relay, opt-out, memory-guard, or broader concurrency work to own the relay pressure cluster.

recommendation.title: Require fail-safe scoping
recommendation.body: Use systemd scoping only after proving the exact constrained scope can start and preserve hook stdio, otherwise keep the original relay command.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent history shows several native hook relay fallback and cleanup changes in the same command/config path.
